name: ThinkingMap
description: One session of thinking. Holds the user's original unstructured idea verbatim and tracks which stage of the loop the session has reached. Everything else hangs off this root, so a saved map can be reopened and continued later. 'revision' is a monotonic counter bumped once per committed change, in the same transaction as the write — it is the cursor an agent reads with and the only shared notion of "now" across all three front doors (in-page WebMCP, HTTP, stdio).

name: Message
description: One turn of the conversation, in order. Nothing in the page renders these any more — the agent lives in the browser, so its conversation is its own and the page cannot see it. They are kept as the record of how a map got started, and an agent calling read_map is given them as context. New thinking is recorded as MapEvent instead. 'origin' records whether the user or the agent produced the turn.

name: MapNode
description: One node in the visual map. A tree via nullable parentId, so no separate edge table is needed. 'kind' says what the node represents (idea, problem, assumption, open-question, research, finding, gap, approach, pro, risk, known, unknown, direction, next-step) and 'status' drives the dashed / solid / highlighted treatment from the mockups. 'origin' says whether the person or the agent contributed it, which is what stops an agent re-ingesting its own writes as new information. Self-referencing, so parents must precede children in seed input order. 'offsetX' / 'offsetY' are an arrangement nudge away from the node's computed tidy position, not a position: the tidy layout stays authoritative, so siblings still never overlap and a node added later still places itself sensibly. They default to 0, and they are deliberately absent from the agent's rendering of the map — arrangement is not thinking.

name: MapEvent
description: The append-only exchange log: every change to a map, agent or human, as one ordered fact. WebMCP is pull-only — a page cannot wake an agent — so the give-and-take has to be a durable record either side can read at any time. One table answers all three forms of "what happened after revision N?": the agent's delta, the inbox of unread user contributions, and the activity feed. It also captures node deletion, which a diff over MapNode rows cannot. 'kind' is one of node.added, node.updated, phase.set, agent.note, question.asked, user.answer, user.note, user.node. 'requestId' is the idempotency key that makes an agent's retry a no-op rather than a duplicate.
